prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website comp at 1536x1024 for a long-form Polyglot Papers article
Primary request: Design the first viewport and the beginning of the second fold for ‘The 12-Hour Routine I Actually Used’ by Aljohn Polyglot.
Structure: a thin familiar shared website navbar at top; below it a full-width night-blue editorial field split 56/44. Left: Polyglot Papers label, May 31 2025, huge condensed sans headline, short readable deck, byline, and a clear ‘Watch the full routine’ action. Right: a giant code-native 24-hour stopwatch dial with 2:00 AM highlighted, seven labeled split ticks, a moving hand, and a compact legend for Recall / Input / Movement / Output / Sleep. Along the bottom of the viewport, a horizontal timing rail begins with the 2:00–5:00 AM block. The next fold begins as an ivory training-log sheet with the first detailed routine block.
Visual world: endurance athlete training log meets analogue stopwatch and coach clipboard. Midnight cobalt occupies roughly half the screen; dawn saffron, track red, daylight ivory, and recovery green mark time periods. Technical paper grain, rubber stamp marks, grease-pencil annotations, precise lane rules. Use a tall condensed grotesque for headlines, neutral readable sans for body, tabular mono for time.
Signature interaction implied: scroll advances the stopwatch hand and active timing split.
Constraints: unmistakably a readable article website, not a poster or app dashboard; real semantic-looking text regions; no serif typography, no glassmorphism, no rounded cards, no gradients, no generic bento grid, no fake testimonials, no invented statistics, no logos beyond Aljohn Polyglot and Polyglot Papers, no watermark.
approvalBasis: User explicitly delegated the visual choice. Comp A was selected because the 24-hour dial explains the routine immediately and leaves the long-form detail readable; the generated portrait and any invented labels are not approved content.
